setup: Lie flat on a mat, arms overhead
execution: Lift arms and legs at the same time
Reach your hands toward your shins
Balance on your hips at the top
faults: Don't throw your arms to get up
Don't arch your back as you lower
Don't let your legs crash down

notes: If your lower back arches as you lower, shorten the range or use the tuck version.
Lower under control; dropping the legs makes the back arch at the bottom.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Hollow body hold
regressions.reason: Hold the bottom shape before adding the fold.

regressions.name: Tuck-up
regressions.reason: Knees bend toward the chest; a shorter lever.

regressions.name: Single-leg V-up
regressions.reason: One leg at a time halves the load.

progressions.name: Toes-to-bar
progressions.reason: Same fold while hanging from a bar.

progressions.name: Weighted V-up
progressions.reason: A light plate or medicine ball in the hands.

substitutions.name: Hanging leg raise
substitutions.reason: Leg-raising with the hips folding, from a bar.

substitutions.name: Cable crunch
substitutions.reason: Loaded trunk flexion on a stack.

substitutions.name: Reverse crunch
substitutions.reason: Lower-body-first curl on the floor; easier to control.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at floor level, head on the left, mat along the floor line, so the V shape and the hips as the pivot are clear.

keyPositions.label: Hover
keyPositions.describe: Lying on the back, arms overhead and legs straight, both just off the mat. Lower back pressed down.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Balanced on the hips and lower back in a V. Straight legs raised about 60–70°, torso raised to meet them, hands reaching beside the shins.

ikHints: Hips stay on the mat as the pivot
emphasise: Arms and legs rise together and meet over the hips
Slow lowering back to the hover
Lower back stays down at the bottom

sources.title: Physitrack: Step-by-step guide to the V-ups exercise
sources.note: Physitrack shows a single-leg, cross-body version; the both-legs version here is the common gym form.

sources.title: ACE Exercise Library: V-Ups

sources.note: ACE describes a seated, bent-knee progression series rather than the full lying V-up.

uncertain.note: The hip flexors do much of the leg lift, so they are listed as primary with the abs (vocabulary word added 23 Oct 2026, expansion research Q1).
"Jackknife sit-up" and "Jackknife crunch" are commonly used for this movement, but some sources use them for a bent-knee version.
Approximate drawing targets, not measured data.
